title: Technical Project Manager - College of Engineering - Engineering Research Accelerator
description:
Carnegie Mellon University is a private, global research university that stands among the world’s most renowned education institutions. With ground-breaking brain science, path-breaking performances, creative start-ups, big data, big ambitions, hands-on learning, and a whole lot of robots, CMU doesn’t imagine the future, we invent it. If you’re passionate about joining a community that challenges the curious to deliver work that matters, your journey starts here!

  

The Engineering Research Accelerator reinforces the College of Engineering’s efforts to expand our participation and influence in national and international research forums, which allows us to develop a stronger platform for our researchers to share our insights and discoveries. We develop deep industry ties and seek new relationships to collaboratively develop solutions to broad problems. These solutions have the potential to create economic value through new products that are useful, usable, and desirable in the marketplace.

The Engineering Research Accelerator is seeking a Technical Project Manager (TPM) to join our team. This role will support federally funded bioengineering / multidisciplinary efforts, influencing the future direction and advancements in bioelectronics at the College of Engineering. The main effort aims to develop a minimally invasive brain-computer interface (BCI) to address hearing loss. Other projects may be assigned based on availability and relevance.

  

The ideal candidate will be a highly motivated and proactive professional who thrives in a dynamic environment, excels at multitasking, and is enthusiastic about joining our team. The Technical Project Manager will provide comprehensive coordination and management support—both administrative and operational—for research projects and initiatives on relevant and assigned complex research awards. This is a dynamic opportunity for someone who thrives in an interesting and challenging work environment. This position regularly handles sensitive matters and requires maintaining strict confidentiality and discretion. This position will also require adaptability and openness to change as the department and organization evolve.

  
  

**Responsibilities:**
=====================

  

**Research Project Administration**

* Assist the Principal Investigators and the research team with timeline and resource management to ensure timely delivery of artifacts and ensure that the project meets the performance goals and milestones.
* Negotiate with stakeholders and apply project management methodologies and best practices.
* Collect and track project updates from research teams and emerging initiatives.
* Create slides and deliverables along with relevant technical personnel. Projects might include but are not limited to data collection, analysis, and dissemination.
* Maintain program websites and draft effective communications with project personnel, campus community, and external stakeholders including sponsors. Serves as the point of contact with sponsors when required of position.
* Facilitate project documentation in digital forms (e.g. spreadsheets, databases, and project management software and collaboration tools). Maintain a repository/catalog of research outputs.
* Tracks and supports research compliance requirements on supported awards including human subjects (IRB) and animal (IACUC) protocols, clinical trials, export controls, and other compliance related requirements.
* Manage risks, implement mitigation strategies, and oversee technology transfer activities.
* Program support may include supporting calls for projects by creating online submission forms, assisting with coordinating web presence for specific programs, and point of contact for submissions, initial reviews and compilation for reviewers.
* Assist with the development of award or project related policies and procedures.
Support coordination of shared resources and facilities as needed by project teams.  

  

**Research Group Mentoring**

* Acts as a liaison between the PI and project team members to provide mentorship and professional guidance to graduate students, undergraduate researchers, and other trainees, including regular one-on-one meetings, feedback on research progress, support with experimental design, data analysis, and review of publications.
* Foster a collaborative and inclusive culture by facilitating research group meetings, coordinating shared workflows, and promoting best practices in data documentation enabling reproducibility of research.
* Advise students on quantitative and qualitative data analysis approaches, reproducibility, and documentation.
* Provide feedback on data interpretation, troubleshooting, and preparation of scientific figures.
* Scientific Communication & Professional Development
* Mentor students in technical writing for fellowships, manuscripts, abstracts, reports, and sponsor communications.
* Support development of oral presentation skills and scientific communication strategies.
* Facilitate a collaborative and inclusive culture through coordinated group workflows and expectations.
Support onboarding of new members, including training on lab processes, safety, documentation, and project-specific procedures.  

  

**Meetings & Events - Coordination and Communications**

* Facilitate program activities and coordinate key meetings and events for the senior project personnel.
* Arrange and attend essential project meetings, take meeting notes, distribute and archive notes along with ensuring that action items are clearly communicated to responsible parties
* Organize events and meetings with faculty, students, industry or government partners, and external collaborators.
Assist with planning and execution of symposiums, workshops, proposal meetings, and public events. Activities include managing logistics and ensuring seamless coordination between research initiatives and internal administrative processes.  

  

**Administrative & Financial Tracking**

* Facilitate agreements processing and administrative processes along with the research administration team at the Engineering Research Accelerator
* Support financial tracking for grant and project budgets along with the Research Administration team/Post Award Financial POC.
Help maintain personnel documentation for supported program portfolios.  

  

Other Duties as Assigned.

  

Flexibility, excellence, and passion are vital qualities within Carnegie Mellon University. Inclusion, collaboration and cultural sensitivity are valued competencies at CMU. Therefore, we are in search of a team member who is able to effectively interact with a varied population of internal and external partners at a high level of integrity. We are looking for someone who shares our values and who will support the mission of the university through their work.

  
  

**Requirements:**
=================

* Masters or PHD degree in Neuroscience, Biomedical Engineering, Computer Science, or a related field with 5 years of experience.
* Willingness to travel to conferences and other meetings/events to collaborate with partners and sponsors.
* Ability to manage multiple competing priorities in a dynamic and uncertain environment.
* Experience coordinating internal and external resources to meet project milestones and deadlines.
* Competence in completing project deliverables on time, within scope, and within budget.
* Skill in defining project scope and objectives, involving relevant stakeholders, and ensuring project feasibility.
* Proven ability to manage relationships with customers and stakeholders.
* Commitment to building and maintaining relationships with a diverse team of colleagues within the College of Engineering and the broader community.
* Strong organizational skills and ability to create and maintain comprehensive project documentation throughout the project lifecycle.
A combination of education and relevant experience from which comparable knowledge is demonstrated may be considered.
